Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances; emit exactly one valid action JSON per turn and infer transformations from demos.

# Continual-ARC

1. On every puzzle turn, obey the action-only protocol: emit exactly one JSON object for `submit` (with grid), `request_demos`, or `finish`, with no narration or tool calls. Read the attempt/demo budgets; `finish` is valid only after the instance is over.
2. Infer the complete rule from demos before submitting. Compare changed cells and dimensions, then test the rule against every pair; validate output row lengths and values. Do not submit a speculative interpretation when a demonstration can resolve it: request one more demo if its expected information is worth its cost, then incorporate that pair before choosing an action.
3. After an incorrect submission, treat feedback only as evidence that the whole grid was wrong; it gives no location. Re-derive the rule from all demos and reconsider dimensions and untouched cells; do not make an unsupported local edit or repeat a guess. Request another demo if available and useful, otherwise submit only a newly evidence-supported result.
